newsitem.title: USA: Foxmeyer asset sale blocked by U.S. court.
newsitem.headline: Foxmeyer asset sale blocked by U.S. court.

text.p: A federal bankruptcy judge refused on Tuesday to approve an agreement for the sale of FoxMeyer Health Corp's assets to McKesson Corp and instead ordered the assets to be auctioned, a creditor attorney source told Reuters.

Chief Judge Helen Balick of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware said at a hearing she would sign an agreement revised to reflect an auction for the sale of the assets, including FoxMeyer Drug Co, the fourth-largest pharmaceutical and health-care products distributor in North America.
A hearing to approve the results of the auction is scheduled before Judge Balick on November 8 at 930 EDT/1330 GMT.
The source told Reuters that a live auction is expected to take place a day or two before the November 8 hearing.
If McKesson does not submit the winning bid, it will still be entitled to a termination payment of $6.5 million.
In court papers, FoxMeyer said "it is essential that the emergency sale be consummated as quickly as possible to ensure that the debtor's assets do not decline further in value."

Last week, McKesson said it agreed to buy the FoxMeyer assets for about $80 million in cash and the assumption of FoxMeyer's liabilities, including its debtor-in- possession financing with G.E. Capital Corp.
